analysis:
Examined both inference-documentation excerpts and the supplied change map. Visible changes describe variable-frame-rate video acceptance using frame-index/nominalFrameRate timestamps (docs/architecture/inference.md:818–823), deterministic processor refusals (837), returned assistant reasoning, strict-tool validation, JSON output withholding and forced-tool post-validation (884–903). These statements alone establish no concrete security regression; implementation controls are outside this batch, not observed missing controls.
For integration, verify GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset bounds work as well as retained decoded bytes for adversarial variable-frame-rate tracks, rejects invalid nominal rates, and preserves private media handling (A-001, TB-007, T-050). Verify GLM5NextResponseFormatOutput and ToolConstraintValidation withhold all invalid answer/tool content on streaming, cancellation and parser-failure paths, including MTP-eligible requests; returned reasoning must remain request-local and must not bypass output-channel encryption (T-007, T-008, T-056). Documentation distinguishes separately streamed reasoning from the validated answer.
Surrounding contracts retain media exclusion from prefix reuse, memory reservations through retirement, receipt-specific cache attribution and actual-token billing. Prompt token reuse is described as scope-bound at 1138–1153, consistent with T-041 account isolation; no changed scope, disk crypto or TTL behavior is evidenced. Attestation, credential custody, privileged fan controls and payment authorization are not changed in these excerpts. The changed weight-hash and later sections listed in the orientation map are outside these primary excerpts and require their own source-pass coverage. Deeper review is needed to reconcile the media and structured-output implementation contracts across supplied PR code; this documentation review does not verify them.
